notes: Documented as the S6L-24D control surface (the current 24-fader flagship in Avid's VENUE | S6L line; the original un-suffixed "S6L-24" was superseded by S6L-24D when the D-series launched). Port list, counts and connector types are essentially identical on the lower-cost S6L-24C sibling (same 8 XLR mic/line in, 8 XLR out, 4 AES3 in, 4 AES3 out, network, USB, MIDI, GPI, LTC, footswitch layout, per Avid's official spec sheet and System Guide) — 24C additionally adds two 3-pin XLR "console lamp" power ports on its top panel (24D instead has a built-in light bar), which are not included here since this profile targets 24D. All connector types/counts/labels were cross-verified against the numbered, labeled rear-panel photo in the official VENUE S6L System Guide (v8.0, 2026) chapter "S6L Control Surface Connections" (pp.89-92), and against Avid's official "VENUE S6L System Specifications" datasheet (AS6LDS0725). Caveats: (1) USB versions differ slightly between Avid's two current official docs — the 2025 datasheet states "5 USB 2.0 (2 front, 2 rear, 1 internal)" while the more recent System Guide specifies the 2 front + 2 rear ports as USB 3.0 and only the 1 internal secure port as USB 2.0; the System Guide's more granular wording was used here. (2) GPI Input/Output are physically 25-pin D-Sub (DB25) male/female connectors; no DB25/D-sub id exists in the allowed connector list, so "rs232" was used as the closest approximation (not an actual RS-232 serial signal — it's parallel logic/relay GPI), consistent with prior entries in this catalog. (3) Network A/B/C/D are AVB Ethernet ports; Avid's AVB/Milan ecosystem is Gigabit-class and Avid explicitly calls the companion Stage 16 I/O rack's AVB ports "Gigabit Ethernet," but the S6L control-surface spec sheet itself never restates a numeric line rate for these ports, so no grade was set (omitted per instructions rather than guessed). (4) LTC Input's XLR3 connector type was confirmed from the labeled rear-panel photo (not spelled out in the guide's prose). (5) Rack unit height omitted — the control surface is a desktop/furniture-style console, not rack-mounted (only the companion E6L engine and Stage I/O racks are rack-mountable).
